content: Now collapse the left-hand side. The urea carbonyl is atom 8 and atom 7 is the NH joining it to the dimethoxybenzyl; that 8-7 bond is non-ring, so cutting it discards the benzyl, the NH and both methoxys in one modification. Putting a methyl on the carbonyl instead turns the urea into a simple acetanilide, giving N-[4-(pyrimidin-2-ylamino)phenyl]acetamide at ~228 Da. Now both NH linkages sit directly on the aromatic ring, which is the comparison I want against ligand 2, and the molecule is small, flat and highly accessible: SA should fall near 1.6 with TPSA around 67.
